Before

On The 4 th Of February, 2026

 Mohd Aamir Khan

The present petition has been preferred under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, assailing the legality, validity and propriety of the order dated 09.01.2026 passed by the learned First Additional Judge to the Court of First Additional Sessions Judge, Gauharganj,
District Raisen in MJCR No. 05/2026, whereby the application submitted by the applicant seeking permission to travel abroad has been rejected.

entities.text:
Court of First Additional Sessions Judge, Gauharganj,
District Raisen
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The facts, in brief, are that on the complaint of Zulekha Usman Gani Patrawala, Police Station Sultanpur, District Raisen registered FIR bearing Crime No. 148/2025 for offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 of the IPC against the present applicant and one Aslam Gani Patrawala (since deceased).

It is alleged that the complainant's son, namely Aslam Gani Patrawala in connivance with the present applicant, prepared forged death certificate of the complainant's mother, on the basis of which a false panchnama was drawn and the land in question was mutated in the name of Aslam Gani Patrawala.

Upon registration of the FIR, the applicant preferred an application seeking anticipatory NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:13594 2 MCRC-1711-2026 bail before this Court, which was dismissed vide order dated 02.07.2025.
Aggrieved thereby, the applicant approached the Hon'ble Apex Court by filing Special Leave Petition (Crl.) No. 9886/2025.

The Hon'ble Apex Court, vide order dated 17.07.2025, was pleased to grant interim protection to the applicant, subject to compliance with the conditions stipulated under Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Subsequently, vide order dated 01.09.2025, the Special Leave Petition was allowed and anticipatory bail was granted to the applicant.
In compliance thereof, the applicant surrendered before the learned Additional Sessions Judge and, upon furnishing requisite bail bonds and surety, was ordered to be released on bail.

While granting bail vide order dated 11.12.2025, the learned Court below imposed certain conditions, inter-alia,

sentences.text: The applicant, being in need of travelling abroad, preferred an application before the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Gauharganj, seeking permission to travel to Dubai for the period from 15.01.2026 to 28.02.2026.

In the said application, it was stated that the applicant intends to purchase a studio apartment in Dubai in contemplation of his daughter's prospective higher studies and, for the said purpose, is required to frequently travel to Dubai for family and related matters.
Along with the application, the applicant furnished copies of his passport, visa, and return air tickets in support of his bona fides.
Upon consideration of the application, the learned Trial Court deemed it appropriate to call for a report from Police Station Sultanpur.

Based on the said report, wherein it was alleged that the applicant had not cooperated during the course of investigation, the learned Trial Court rejected the application preferred by the applicant seeking permission to travel abroad vide order dated NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:13594 3 MCRC-1711-2026 09.01.2026.Being aggrieved by the said order passed by the learned Trial Court, the applicant has preferred the present petition before this Hon'ble Court.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant contends that the learned Trial Court has committed a manifest error in rejecting the application seeking permission to travel abroad.
It is submitted that the Court below has mechanically relied upon the police report, which is based on erroneous and misconceived facts, without independently assessing the material on record.

It is further urged that the applicant has been duly cooperating with the investigation, as is evident from the orders of the Hon'ble Supreme Court granting protection subject to compliance with stipulated conditions, which the applicant has scrupulously adhered to.
The impugned order, therefore, suffers from non-application of mind and has been passed in disregard of settled legal principles.
Emphasis is laid on the proposition that the right to travel abroad is an integral facet of personal liberty under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

It is submitted that once bail has been granted and the applicant has faithfully complied with all imposed conditions, his request for temporary permission to travel abroad ought to be considered on its own merits.

The presence of the applicant can adequately be secured by imposing appropriate safeguards, such as furnishing additional surety,
disclosing itinerary and assets, or any other condition deemed fit by this Hon'ble Court.

On the aforesaid grounds, it is prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to set aside the impugned order dated 09.01.2026 passed by the learned First Additional Sessions Judge, Gauharganj, District Raisen, in MJCR No. 05/2026, and further be pleased to permit the applicant to travel to Dubai from 15.01.2026 to 28.02.2026, in the interest of justice.

entities.text: First Additional Sessions Judge, Gauharganj, District Raisen
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
4. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer made by learned counsel for the petitioner and has supported NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:13594 4 MCRC-1711-2026 the impugned order.
It is submitted that the order passed by the Court below does not call for any interference by this Court in the exercise of its jurisdiction.
Accordingly, a prayer has been made for dismissal of the present petition.

5. Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record Mohd Aamir Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85995870/
2 6.

sentences.text: Upon perusal of the record, it is revealed that the applicant is facing criminal trial and is one of the accused in the said case.
It further transpires that the applicant has a criminal antecedent.
Apart therefrom, no sufficient material has been placed on record to demonstrate that the proposed visit of the applicant abroad is essential or unavoidable.

7. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, this Court does not find any illegality, perversity,
or jurisdictional error in the impugned order whereby the application preferred by the applicant seeking permission to travel abroad has been rejected.

8. Accordingly, the present petition, being devoid of merits, stands dismissed (HIMANSHU JOSHI)
JUDGE (ra)
